EXPLANATION: The spectrum is dominated by aliphatic C–H stretches at 2880, 2937, and 2980 cm⁻¹, consistent with a saturated chain (GFQ-003). A weak band at 2812 cm⁻¹ is characteristic of the aldehydic C–H Fermi resonance near ~2720–2820 cm⁻¹, supporting an aldehyde. Mid-frequency bands at 1458 and 1491 cm⁻¹ are consistent with CH₂/CH₃ deformations (GFQ-003), and skeletal C–C/C–C–C modes near 1066 and 1121 cm⁻¹ match long-chain aliphatic profiles. The 839 cm⁻¹ feature can be assigned to an aldehydic CH out-of-plane bend. Options with nitro/nitrite (10) or CF₃ (7) would require strong group-specific bands (e.g., ~1650 or ~1520 cm⁻¹) that are absent, and candidates with ≡C–H (5) or Si–H/Si–Cl (6) are incompatible with the observed regions. Among aldehydes, a straight-chain saturated aldehyde (heptanal) best matches the overall pattern; the missing C=O band (~1720 cm⁻¹) can be weak in Raman or below detection in this dataset.
